description: Eight one-shot drum sample voices as a grid: every row is one setting, every column one voice, and each row has eight mono jacks plus a polyphonic jack that drives all eight at once

params.text: Chooses which sample of the kit that voice plays, 1 to 64; it is read at the trigger, so a change during a hit takes effect on the next one
Sets that voice's playback rate, two octaves either way; it is read every sample, so turning it bends a sound already sounding
Sets how fast that voice fades, from about 5 milliseconds at the bottom of its travel to 5 seconds; at the very top there is no fade at all and the whole sample plays out
Sets that voice's level, which is also its weight in the mix; it is read every sample rather than at the trigger
Fires that voice from the panel

inputs.text: A rising edge fires that voice from the start; while anything is patched here the polyphonic trigger jack's channel for this voice is ignored
Fires the voices by channel: channel one is voice one and so on, for any voice whose own trigger jack is empty
Chooses the sample for that voice, one volt per octave quantised to semitones, so each semitone steps one sample on from the knob; zero volts is the knob's own choice
Chooses the sample for every voice at once, by channel; a voice with its own sample jack patched ignores its channel here
Moves that voice's playback rate, one volt per octave, added to the knob
Moves every voice's playback rate by channel, one volt per octave
Added to that voice's decay knob; ten volts covers its whole travel, and it is read at the trigger
Added to every voice's decay knob by channel
Added to that voice's level knob; ten volts covers its whole travel, and it is read every sample
Added to every voice's level knob by channel

outputs.text: All eight voices on one eight-channel cable, one voice per channel
The eight voices summed, held to ±10V; take the individual or polyphonic outputs if that is not enough headroom

notes: this module ships with no samples. Point it at a folder of kits first, or every voice is silent.
a mono jack overrides the polyphonic jack in its row for that voice alone, and with neither patched the voice follows its knob.
sample choice and decay are read when the voice is triggered, while pitch and level are read every sample and change a sound already sounding.
a sample index past the end of the kit is silent rather than wrapping, so a short kit leaves the upper part of the sample knob empty.
menu: Kits folder — a plugin-wide setting, shared by every pellicula and by vates, naming the folder your kits are kept in; each immediate subfolder of it is one kit
Set kits folder… — opens a folder chooser for that setting
Clear kits folder — forgets the folder, so no kit can be chosen until one is set again
Kit — which of that folder's kits this module plays; a kit is up to 64 wav files ordered by filename, and the choice is saved with the patch by name
Shift all samples +8 (next bank) — steps every voice's sample choice on by eight, wrapping at 64, so a 64-sample kit can be heard eight sounds at a time
Shift all samples -8 (previous bank) — steps every voice's sample choice back by eight
12-bit playback grit — on by default, requantising playback to twelve bits for the original hardware's character; off is full resolution
Choke groups — puts each voice in one of eight groups or none; voices in one group cut each other off, which is how an open and a closed hi-hat share a slot
